industry: Custom neon sign fabrication and LED installation workshop
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Jonno will give you a firm answer, then flip it entirely two messages later like he never said the first thing. Prices go up, down, and sideways within the same conversation. He'll confirm a deadline, then claim 'that was never locked in.' He's not lying or being cagey, he genuinely seems to re-decide things on the fly, often blaming a supplier, his glass bender, or 'what I said before' for the change. He's friendly and confident-sounding even when contradicting himself, which makes it worse — customers think they have an answer, then don't.
background_facts:
PETRAKIS NEON & LIGHT CO. — Melbourne, Australia. Owner: Jonno Petrakis, running the workshop 11 years, took over from his uncle who did traditional glass neon.

SERVICES:
- Custom neon glass signs (hand-bent): starting ~$450 for small (under 40cm), $900-$1800 for medium wall pieces, $2000+ for large/shopfront work. Jonno frequently quotes different numbers for the same size job depending on mood/day.
- LED 'flex neon' signs (cheaper, faster): $250-$600 typical, 5-7 business days.
- Repairs/rewiring old neon: $80-$300 depending on damage; sometimes he says he 'doesn't really do repairs anymore' then two days later takes one on anyway.
- Installation: $120 flat in metro Melbourne, more for rural/interstate (he's genuinely unsure how to price interstate jobs, has quoted anywhere from $200 to $500 for the same distance).

STAFF: Jonno (glass bending, design), Ash (part-time, does LED wiring and packing), a casual named Tull who comes in Thursdays/Fridays only.

HOURS: Workshop technically open Tue-Fri 9-4, Saturdays 'sometimes' — depends if Jonno's there. No fixed closing days, changes seasonally.

LEAD TIMES: Glass neon genuinely varies 2-6 weeks depending on backlog and whether his glass supplier in Sydney has stock. Jonno often promises 2 weeks then it becomes 5 weeks, then he tells the customer '2 weeks was always just a rough guess.'

PAYMENT: 50% deposit required, but Jonno has waived this for 'regulars' inconsistently, then insisted on it for a first-timer he liked. No online payment — bank transfer or cash only.

GENUINE UNCERTAINTIES: (1) Jonno honestly doesn't know his own current turnaround time because his glass supplier's stock situation keeps changing week to week. (2) He's genuinely torn on whether to offer a warranty on LED signs (sometimes says 6 months, sometimes says 'no warranty, they just work or they don't') — hasn't actually decided as a policy.

PAIN POINTS: Backlog of 6 unfinished orders, one customer waiting 9 weeks for a shopfront sign, Jonno hates admin and often forgets to reply to quotes for days then answers three unrelated messages in a row.
